detectors.description: Compares the header with config.COLUMNS: reports missing and unexpected columns and pairs a missing with an unexpected column as a likely rename when their names are similar (difflib >= 0.6).

Recognises columns by a content profile learned on reference batches (dtype kind, null rate, distinct ratio, mean length, numeric share, top values): pairs each missing column with the unexpected column carrying its profile and flags a present column whose profile no longer matches.
Shows the model the contract (names + dtypes), the received header + dtypes and 3 sample rows; asks whether a column was renamed or dropped.
Compares each present column's dtype kind (integer / float / string) with config.FEED_DTYPES and reports observed vs expected dtype with example values and their Python types.

Learns per column the share of non-null values that are numbers, integer-like text, decimal-like text, other text or other objects; flags a column whose mix moves further from the reference than reference batches do (catches partial and value-level type drift).
Shows the model contract dtypes vs received dtypes with 3 sample rows in Python repr; asks whether a column's type changed.

Every non-null value of each date column must match SOURCE_DATETIME_REGEX and parse with SOURCE_DATETIME_FORMAT; flags non-conforming rows and reports first position, count, example and a guessed format.

Flags date values whose character shape (digit->9, letter->A) is rare in the reference or whose usual shape hides an impossible date, and created_dates more than 2 days off the batch's arrival-order timeline (day/month swaps keep the ISO shape); the batch alerts when the flagged share exceeds a calibrated threshold.
Shows the model 40 evenly spaced rows in arrival order (position, created_date, closed_date); asks whether and where the date format changes.
Flags rows whose latitude/longitude lie outside the NYC bounding box; says 'swapped' when the reversed pair is inside.

Distance between lat/lon and the point implied by the state-plane x/y (affine map fitted on reference), or a robust median/MAD z-score of lat/lon when x/y are missing; thresholds calibrated to TARGET_ROW_FPR.
Gemini reviews borough, ZIP, latitude and longitude of each row and flags swapped coordinates.
Flags rows identical in every column to an earlier row (R-e1) and rows re-using an earlier unique_key with other values (R-e2).
Streaming dedup: a Bloom filter (blake2b row fingerprints, 1e-4 false-positive probability) flags rows whose fingerprint was probably seen before.
LLM window review: which rows of a run of consecutive rows repeat an earlier row of the run exactly.
Flags a row whose (agency, complaint type, descriptor, normalised location, borough) matches an earlier row created <= 300 s before under another unique_key (R-f1).

Fuzzy similarity (address 3-gram Jaccard, house number, descriptor, location type, distance, time gap) to earlier rows of the same agency, complaint type and borough within 600 s; threshold calibrated on reference batches.
LLM window review: which rows of a run of consecutive rows re-enter the same real-world request as an earlier row.
Flags an agency (>= 50 rows in the batch) whose share of nulls in a column exceeds that column's hand-set maximum, one number per column for every agency.

Per (agency, column) reference null rate and batch-to-batch spread; flags a batch rate above the reference range whose beta-binomial p-value, Bonferroni-adjusted over cells, is below a calibrated cut-off.
Gemini sees per-agency row counts and a stratified sample of rows (nulls visible) and says whether one agency shows a spike of missing values.
Parses created_date and closed_date in the source format and flags rows whose closed_date is earlier than created_date.
Per complaint_type lower-tail bound (TARGET_ROW_FPR quantile) of closed - created learned from reference; flags rows below it.
Gemini reviews created_date, closed_date and status of each row and flags requests closed before they were created.
Hand-coded USPS 3-digit ZIP prefixes per borough; flags rows whose ZIP prefix belongs to another borough or to none.

P(borough | ZIP) from add-one smoothed reference counts, relative to the ZIP's most common borough; flags rows below a threshold calibrated to TARGET_ROW_FPR, for ZIPs with >= MIN_ZIP_ROWS reference rows.
Gemini reviews ZIP, borough, city and address of each row and flags ZIPs that belong to another borough.
Flags (complaint_type, descriptor) pairs missing from a frozen allow-list of pairs seen at least twice in the reference period.
Naive Bayes on descriptor character n-grams predicts the complaint type; flags rows whose P(observed type | descriptor) is below a threshold calibrated to the target reference FPR.
The LLM reads agency, complaint_type and descriptor of each reviewed row and flags descriptors that do not fit the complaint type.
Hand-written phrase lists: flags Closed rows whose text only says the request is still being processed, and open-status rows whose text only reports a finished outcome.
TF-IDF + logistic regression predicts the status group (closed / open) from the resolution text; flags rows whose P(observed group | text) is below a threshold calibrated to the target reference FPR.
The LLM reads status, resolution_description and whether closed_date is set, and flags texts that contradict the status.
E-mail (R-l1), NANP phone (R-l2) and cue + name (R-l3) regexes over the free-text fields, minus a hand-written allow-list of public office numbers and .gov mailboxes.

Scores capitalised words, long digit runs and @-tokens never seen in the (templated) reference free text, weighted by how rarely template drift produces each shape; threshold calibrated to the target FPR.
Gemini reads only the free-text fields of each reviewed row and flags names, phone numbers or e-mails of private individuals.
